messages.content: Write a polished short scene in modern American English between two adult friends who disagree about something important but ordinary. Let them disagree naturally without turning the conversation into a dramatic argument. Use realistic dialogue, interruptions, pauses, small physical actions, and a little personality. Neither character should suddenly become cruel or completely change their behavior. Let the disagreement remain unresolved for now. Avoid melodrama, clichés, and narrator explanations.

“I just think you should wait.”

Alex looked across the table. “I've been waiting for three weeks.”

“I know.”

“So what changes tomorrow?”

Jordan sighed and folded the corner of the receipt she was holding. “Nothing. I just think you should sleep on it.”

“I have slept on it.”

“Once.”

“Twice.”

“That isn't the point.”

Alex leaned back. “Then what's the point?”

Jordan opened her mouth, then stopped.

“I don't know,” she said.

Alex's expression softened a little. “Okay.”

“I just don't want you making a decision because you're angry.”

“I'm not angry.”

Jordan gave her a look.

“Fine,” Alex said. “I'm a little angry.”

“A little?”

“Don't push it.”

Jordan smiled despite herself. “There you are.”

Alex shook her head. “You're impossible.”

“And you're stubborn.”

“I've heard that before.”

“I've said it before.”

They sat quietly for a moment.

Alex picked up the receipt Jordan had been folding and flattened it against the table.

“I still haven't decided,” she said.

Jordan nodded. “Good.”

“I'm probably going to.”

“I know.”

Alex slid the receipt back across the table.

“We're going to argue about this again, aren't we?”

“Absolutely.”

“Thought so.””
